discipline: Formal methods and knowledge representation (AI-written). Read: the 15 places, all 88 decisions, the checkers' remarks, draw.py and layout.json, the three earlier proposals' comparison, premises.json, situations.json, families A and E in dynamics.json, and the Lean statements of about 30 laws behind the decisions (RuleCapture, ClosedCapture, ReadInTime, ReadOffInTime, RuleShaping, DrawnShaping, PoolFromCourse, SharedCodes, Attraction, Branching). Counts below come from small read-only scripts; nothing was built or run in Lean.
verdict_on_present:
What it gets right: a place is a condition with a test, not a verdict; every mark was settled against a Lean statement, with the evidence kept and a second reader set to refute it; strength is drawn; unresolved items are kept; the names are plain; overlap is admitted. A person looked and saw a map. Keep all of that.

As a PICTURE at 15 boxes it is not shown to be dominated: the five-minute read is what Ren said yes to, and no design argument outranks that.

As a STORE it is dominated. The cause is one thing: the Lean's state is a product and its laws have several typed inputs, and the store flattens both. In ClosedCapture the configuration is ((share, what lies beyond it), rule); in the Readers section it is share x (rule x judging). `Locked` is a predicate on (share, rule); `Unread` and `ReadsShare` are predicates on the law, fixed along a run; `ReadableInTime <-> T < N` is an order of two steps. A flat place list has one slot for all three kinds, and an arrow between two places has one tail for a law with four hypotheses of different kinds (ReadInTime.turned_iff: the loss accrues; who is pooled; two rebuildings running; the count at that step). The seven points in the next field are the consequences, each with items.

A store with typed answers and laws as rows can regenerate the v1 picture (named combinations as boxes, laws as arrows) and also the other projections; v1 cannot regenerate them. That is the sense in which it is dominated. The price is more curation per law (see cost).
dominated_where: FAITHFULNESS, one mark for three logical forms. Of the 38 arrows, 18 rest on an iff, 8 on one built case, 3 on no law. Nine of the iffs (marked both_ways) have no step in them at all: RuleShaping.favours_iff is `favours (shaped a s p c) <-> c <= s`, a closed statement about parameters (shaping-the-rule... transitions 1, 2, 4, 5; shaping-read... transition 2; offspring-read... transitions 1, 2; unselected-beyond... exits 1, 6). They are drawn as arrows between places. The checkers said it themselves: 'never show a rule passing from one side to the other in time'; 'no law here is of a course of cohorts'. A movement is drawn that no law shows.

FAITHFULNESS, strength of a bundle. draw.py takes the best strength among the items on a pair (`best = min(items, key=rank)`). uncounted -> felt is drawn 'exact' from three iffs that are borders or a clock order (readableInTime_iff, separates_all_iff_member, readOffCouplings_alike_iff) plus two built cases. No law shows, exactly, a loss coming to be felt.

FAITHFULNESS, 'comes to'. closed-capture exits 1 and 2 and a-counter-rule exit 2 are drawn judged-inside -> cost-counts / holds-itself -> cost-counts with the condition 'the rule comes to register what is used up'. ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss has neither `Locked` nor the readers among its hypotheses, and 'the rule read favours at no configuration whose loss is at least N' is its PREMISE. What moves in the law is the loss passing N. The change from a rule that does not count the loss to one that does is a change of setup that no law in the region gives.

TOPOLOGY, the centre. The report 'no law gives an arrow INTO the hold' is an artifact of the list, not a fact of the Lean. RuleCapture.uniform_locks takes ANY configuration to `Locked` by the step after the second rebuilding (capture-through-the-rule transition 1, filed 'inside' because no place exists for its source). Six arrows conclude `forall k, Locked ...` in Lean and are drawn into other boxes: readers-drawn exit 1 and transition 2; shaping-read exit 1; loss-read-in-time exit 1, transitions 1 and 2. Further, the 88 items are exits by construction, so mechanism laws that arrive (favouring_locks, DrawnShaping.drawn_locks) are not items at all.

USE, free-text tests. Three independent readers placing the 88 items agreed on 37, two of three on 32, split on 19 (compare.json). Tests lean on capitals (NOT, AND, BECAUSE, NOTHING). A person locating a real case faces the same ambiguity, and with 40 places there are 780 pairs to keep apart instead of 105.

ECONOMY and said-once. Five decision kinds plus 22 distinct free-text `kind` strings; the relations between places ('a case of', 'with') and nine arrow labels are stored in layout.json, the drawing file, traceable to no law. One law drawn as two arrows to two boxes: ClosedCapture.Thinned.kept_iff is both felt -> cost-counts and felt -> past-turning-back.

SUBJECT missing. A place does not say whose condition it is. Checkers: 'the map needs to say whose agreement a node is' (SharedCodes.AgreeAt takes a group G); 'ended' is used for a dependant ending while the rule and those ahead go on.

NOT DUALISTIC. cost-counts has 8 arrows in and 0 out; past-turning-back 5 in, 0 out; ended 2 in, 0 out. The picture has termini, one named as the good outcome and two as bad. In Lean the first two are the same predicate: `Locked order favours` and `Locked (reverse order) disfavours`. Also cost-counts merges 'not favoured at the next step' (turned_by_loss) with 'held the other way from then on' (turned_iff); a checker found a course that satisfies the first and is then kept for the old side for good.

SCALING. Overlap is the rule, not the exception: judged-inside = holds-itself with uncounted and a third condition; shaping-pays and shaping-costs each coincide with a side of holds-itself at the tipping count; noticers-gone overlaps all-on-one, uncounted and felt; felt and past-turning-back differ only by timing. Flat places multiply with every new aspect; a checker already found a cell that 'fits none of the three tests' (ClosedCapture.lock_outlives_loss: held, with an unread loss growing, readers unspecified).
proposal_in_one_paragraph: Store laws, not places. Keep a short list of QUESTIONS one can ask of anything (about seven for this region: how is the rule made; is the lead held, and for which side; whom does what is used up outside the count reach; who has a say; which comes first; how many ways are in use; does it go on), each with a few typed ANSWERS tied to the Lean predicate and the ledger premises. Each LAW is one row: the answers it is given, the answers it then shows, and its shape (kept, arrives, exactly-when, border, clock, by chance, one built case, a reading). A PLACE is not stored: it is any combination of answers, which is the theory's own notion (family A: a region R : S -> Prop, `Absorbing`, `DrawnInto`, juncture), so overlap and nesting are just sets. A name such as 'judged only from inside' is a label on a combination. A CHANGE is a law whose `then` differs from its `given`; a border is not a change. A REAL CASE is the same questions answered, with 'not known' allowed. From this, two things are drawn: an area map per region (answers as areas that nest and touch; an exactly-when law is the border between two areas; an arrow only where a law has a course crossing; a closed outline where a law keeps a run inside; a strip for which-comes-first; blank where no law speaks), and the case sheet (the questions as a form; answering it marks where the case is, which laws now apply, which are one answer away, what is unanswered). The v1 node-link picture stays available as a third drawing of the same store.
schema:
Four tables; everything else is computed.

question
- id
- ask: the question in plain words, at most 12 (en, zh).
- of: whose condition it is (the rule; those ahead; those who bear what is used up; those with a say; a dependant; a group).
- ranges_over: `state` (a configuration at a step), `setup` (the law or a parameter, fixed along a run) or `clock` (the order of two steps). Read from which bound variables the Lean hypothesis mentions.

answer
- id, question
- label: plain, en and zh.
- lean: the predicate(s) with arguments, e.g. Becoming.RuleCapture.Locked(side, reading).
- premises: ledger ids, e.g. rulecapture-locked, closedcapture-unread.
- within: an answer this one is a case of (nesting).
- joined_by: the Lean lemma that identifies predicates from two modules under this answer, or 'a reading' if none.

law
- lean: the declaration name; this is the row's id.
- dynamic, item: the atlas exit, transition or compose it belongs to; null for a mechanism law.
- given: list of answers (and 'any' where the statement quantifies over every start).
- then: list of answers.
- shape: kept | arrives | exactly-when (a branch with an exact guard) | border (an iff with no step in it) | clock | by-chance (a bound on weight) | one-built-case | reading.
- when: from then on | by step n | at the next step | never.
- strength: the atlas's (exact, sufficient, necessary, witness).
- drops: ledger premise ids an exit drops (already in dynamics.json).
- reach: any type | any process | World | the named model.
- plain: one sentence, at most 25 words (en, zh).

case
- id, web: formations, conditions, couplings, readers (as situations.json has them).
- answers: question -> answer or 'not known', each with why and source.
- premises: assessed met / not checked / fails (already there).

Computed, not stored
- place: a combination of answers. name: {answers, label, known_as} for combinations worth a name; v1's 15 labels move here.
- hole: an answer that appears in no law's `then`; two touching answers with no law between.
- next(case): laws whose `given` the case's answers meet; one_away(case): laws missing one answer.

A place is a region (a set of answers). A change is a law whose `then` differs from its `given` in at least one question. A real case is an answer sheet; where little is known its position is a large region, and that is shown.
drawn_from_it:
1. THE REGION SHEET, an area map (statechart conventions: nesting for 'a case of', side-by-side panels for independent questions).
- Areas are the answers of the one or two questions the region turns on; at most about seven visible. Overlap is drawn as overlap, nesting as inside.
- A border between touching areas carries the law that divides them exactly (shape border or exactly-when), written on the border. Nothing moves across it in the drawing.
- An arrow crosses from one area to another only where a law has a course doing so (arrives, exactly-when). Its guard is the other questions' answers, as small marks keyed to their panel. 'From any start' is an arrow from the enclosing area's edge inward.
- A closed outline means a law keeps a run inside (kept). An open outline means no such law.
- A strip under the sheet holds clock laws: two marks and what each order gives.
- One built case and by-chance are dotted, with 'one case' or the bound beside them. A reading is grey. Blank means no law speaks.
- Four drawn marks in the legend: border, arrow, outline, dotted path.
For this region two panels carry about 40 of the 88 items: (a) the hold, on a line of 'cost of bending the rule against what comes back' with two marks, the hold for each side as two areas divided by the tipping count; (b) a time strip with two marks, 'first shows on someone with a say' and 'no return', joined to (a) by the branch on counts.

2. THE CASE SHEET. The same questions, in the same order, as a form of about seven lines. Filled in, it shades the case's areas on the sheet and lists: laws that now apply (with strength), laws one answer away (what would have to change), and questions unanswered.

Articles follow from the same tables, one per answer (about 20 for this region) and one per named combination: the question it answers, what the laws show given it, how one comes to be here, what it borders, what no law shows, cases found here, known as. Only the lead and the example are written by hand.
worked_sample:
QUESTIONS for the region (ranges_over in brackets)
- rule [setup]: set from outside | rebuilt from its own results {leans one way at every count | has a tipping count} | rebuilt against its results. Lean: ReadsShare; `uniform`; ReadsShare on reverse M.
- hold [state]: held for side A | held for side B | not held. Lean: Locked M favours h p; Locked (reverse M) disfavours; Alternating.never_locked.
- out [state and setup]: what is used up outside the count reaches no one with a say (Unread, Accrues) | someone with a say | those ahead themselves (bear l 0) | the rule counts it (`turns`).
- say [state]: those ahead only | others too, fewer | others too, no fewer | those who would notice removed.
- first [clock]: shows before no return (T < N) | not before; removed before they register (K <= N).
- bend [setup]: cost at most what the others see returning (c <= lo) | between | at least what the benders see (hi <= c).
- ways [state, of a group G]: several | one (AgreeAt G).

SEVEN PLACES re-expressed
1. holds-itself = {rule: own results, hold: held, either side}. Says nothing on `out`.
2. judged-inside = {rule: own results, say: those ahead only, hold: held, out: no one with a say}. No single law has all four: readers_uniform_locks gives the first three, lock_outlives_loss gives hold with out. The name marks itself 'two laws read together', which is what both checkers asked the test to say.
3. The cell the checkers could not place (lock_outlives_loss; a-counter-rule exit 2's origin) = {rule: own results, hold: held, out: no one with a say, say: unsaid}. No new place is needed.
4. uncounted = {out: no one with a say}, whatever the hold.
5. past-turning-back is two things: (a) {hold: held for A, from then on, out: someone with a say} (ReadInTime.kept_early_iff, deadline, kept_past_least: all conclude `forall k, Locked order favours`), a law of one named model; (b) {first: not before no return} (ReadOffInTime too_late_of_alike: concludes not ReadableInTime, with no rule and no hold in the statement), a general law. No Lean lemma joins them: joined_by = a reading.
6. cost-counts is three things: {hold: held for B, from then on} (turned_iff, turned_early_iff); {hold: not for A, at the next step} (turned_by_loss); and a measure taken over a fixed list (selection-read-off-its-own-survivors exit 1).
7. shaping-pays, shaping-costs = {bend: c <= lo}, {bend: hi <= c}: answers about the setup, not states anything moves between.

TEN LAWS re-expressed (dynamic, item; v1 decision; then the row)
a. capture-through-the-rule, transition 1; v1 'inside holds-itself'. RuleCapture.uniform_locks. given {rule: own results, leans one way; hold: any}; then {hold: held}; shape arrives; when: by the step after the second rebuilding; sufficient, bound tight (Second.second_exact).
b. loss-read-in-time-by-the-others, exit 1; v1 felt -> cost-counts. ReadInTime.turned_iff. given {hold: rule in force for A; out: reaches the others' judging; two rebuildings running; pooled judging goes against A at r}; then {hold: held for B, from r+2 on}; shape exactly-when: the pooled judging at r+1 still goes against A, ties included.
c. same dynamic, transition 1; v1 felt -> past-turning-back. kept_early_iff. Same given; then {hold: held for A, from N+1 on}; exactly-when the pooled judging, loss included, favours A at N. b and c are one branch with two outcomes, both the hold.
d. same dynamic, transition 2; v1 felt -> past-turning-back. deadline. shape clock: the others begin counting no earlier than a step fixed by the starting counts; then {hold: held for A, from then on}; sufficient ('a bound, not the step at which the window closes').
e. closed-capture, exit 1; v1 judged-inside -> cost-counts. ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss. given {out: grows every step; out: the rule counts it}; then {hold: not for A}; when: at the step after each rebuilding once the loss has passed N. Its tail is every configuration with those two answers, the centre among them but not only it.
f. shaping-the-rule-selected-by-what-comes-back, transition 1; v1 arrow both ways. RuleShaping.favours_iff. shape border between {bend: covered} and {bend: not covered}. No step.
g. shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected, transition 1 (v1 'inside') and transition 2 (v1 arrow). DrawnShaping.favours_everywhere_iff (c <= lo and c <= hi), critical_mass_iff (lo < c < hi), disfavours_strictly_everywhere_iff (lo < c and hi <= c). One line of c with two marks: left of lo, one hold for the benders from every count; between, two holds divided by a count; from hi, one hold against them.
h. the-lock-draws-its-readers-out, exit 3; v1 'leads-out', unplaced by three readers three ways. PoolFromCourse.borne_by_shapers_favours_iff: favours <-> c + l <= s. It is border f moved by the loss l. {out: falls on those ahead themselves} lands on a line already drawn.
i. reading-a-loss-in-time, transition 1 and exits 1, 2; v1 three arrows. readableInTime_iff (<-> T < N), too_late_of_alike. shape clock: one strip, two marks, two orders.
j. the-lock-draws-its-readers-out, transition 1; v1 'stays in noticers-gone'. window_never_read. given {hold: held; out: grows; first: removed before they register, K <= N}; then {hold: held; out: past every bound}; shape kept. In Lean it is a law of the hold, guarded by a clock.
k. shaping-read..., exit 2; v1 holds-itself -> all-on-one. DrawnReplacement.lost_ge. shape by-chance: a lower bound on the weight of runs; then {ways: one}.

See what_it_reveals for what this shows that the flat map does not.
what_it_reveals:
1. ARRIVALS at the hold. Laws a, b, c, d and j conclude `Locked`. By a rough scan of the laws the 88 decisions cite, 16 items cite a law whose conclusion contains `Locked` (7 filed inside, 6 drawn as arrows to other boxes, 3 as stays). The centre is the best-connected condition in the Lean, not an island.

2. A LOOP where v1 has a terminus. Law b ends in `Locked (reverse order) disfavours`: turning the hold lands in the hold, for the other side, under a reading that now counts that loss. Every law given {hold: held} then applies again with the sides exchanged: locked_stays, perturbation_absorbed and lock_outlives_loss are stated for any orders and any `favours`, and ReadsShare.reverse is the lemma for the exchange. So the picture is hold(A) -> hold(B) -> whatever B's reading does not count, with no end state named for a good outcome. How far seen: argued from the statements' generality; I found no theorem that states it for the turned hold and built nothing.

3. Two HOLES, computed not noticed. (i) The answers of `rule` appear only in `given`: no law in the region shows a rule set from outside coming to be rebuilt from its results. The three laws that conclude ReadsShare (threshold_reads, weighted_reads, Drawn.pool_reads) show that a model has it, not that a rule comes to have it; the atlas's own open note says the same. (ii) {out: the rule counts it} is only ever a premise (`turns`). v1 draws (ii) as three solid arrows (law e and its two siblings). The two changes that matter most for alignment in this region are changes of setup that no law here gives. That is worth drawing as blank.

4. A DEPENDENCY. Eleven items are one line with two marks: the seven both-ways 'arrows' between shaping-pays and shaping-costs, the three critical-mass items filed inside holds-itself, and unplaced item h. shaping-pays, shaping-costs and the two sides of holds-itself are the three segments of that line. v1 shows three boxes and a note.

5. One law, one mark. kept_iff (two arrows in v1) and the pair b, c become one branch each.
loses_or_risks:
- The five-minute picture is NOT established for this proposal. Panels with guard marks can read as 'connections between components', the thing Ren rejected. The area drawing is my mitigation; only his read settles it. If it reads worse, keep v1's drawing and take only the store.
- Manufactured unity is the main risk. Two modules' predicates are not one predicate because they share a word: past-turning-back joins a general law with a named-model law by a reading; ChoiceCountCapture's lock is its own statement. Each answer must carry `joined_by` (a Lean lemma, or 'a reading'), or the schema will show joins the Lean does not have. The atlas has only 10 compose entries, so many joins will be marked readings.
- A product of questions invites combinations no law speaks of. Blank must read as 'nothing shown', never as possible or impossible.
- Vocabulary moves, it does not vanish: seven question wordings and four drawn marks to learn, against 15 place names and four line styles. Shapes in the store are eight; I would draw four.
- The story thins. v1 reads left to right as one account. The structured map needs one case walked through it to carry the argument.
- Laws of one named model (38 of 183 dynamics) look general on any chart unless `reach` is drawn. v1 has the same fault.
- More curation per law: `given` and `then` over several questions, where v1 needed one from and one to.
- My counts of law shapes used a rough text parser (it missed about 9 of about 75 cited laws: non-ASCII names, other namespaces). Treat the 18 and the 16 as close, not exact.
cost_to_build:
DERIVED BY SCRIPT from what exists
- The law rows: dynamics.json already lists 2,181 law entries with the premises each takes, across 177 dynamics; 207 of 321 exits carry `drops`; transitions carry `declarations` and `kind`.
- Shape, first draft: transitions' kind (atlas-wide: exact threshold 29, tipping in a parameter 23, critical mass 5 -> border or exactly-when; window or deadline 22, pace bound 9 -> clock; exit by drift 4 -> by chance) and exits' strength (witness 160 of 321 -> one built case). From the Lean statement: conclusion is an iff; no hypotheses (a built case); `forall k` in the conclusion (from then on); the same predicate in hypothesis and conclusion (kept).
- ranges_over (state, setup, clock): from which bound variables a hypothesis mentions (the configuration; f and h; numerals; `reads`, N, K).
- answer -> Lean and ledger: premises.json has `lean` names for all 1,669; `holds_in` for 145 and `fails_in` for 124.
- Holes, next(case), one_away(case), the article skeletons, and v1's picture as a fallback drawing.
An exact version of the statement reading is a small Lean program that prints each cited declaration's binders and conclusion. It needs one build: machine time, Ren's to release. The text parser is enough to draft.

CURATED BY READING
- Grouping premises into answers. Region: 291 premises taken by 20 dynamics, 52 shared by two or more -> about 20 answers under 7 questions. Atlas: 1,652 taken, 355 shared by two or more dynamics; my estimate, not measured, is 12 to 15 questions and 45 to 60 answers.
- `of`, `joined_by`, the plain labels and questions in both languages, and names for combinations.
- `given` and `then` per law, checked against the statement. The 88 decisions are not wasted: from, to and place are first drafts, `evidence` already quotes the statement, and `condition_en` is the `plain` sentence. The pass now proposing places for the other families can produce answers under questions with the same reading.
- The case: situations.json's one case needs its seven answers; 36 of its 40 premises are 'not checked', so most answers will be 'not known', and the sheet will say so.
scales_to_other_families:
E, Waiting and reciprocity (10 dynamics): holds, and shows the same shapes as C. Questions: which law of giving [setup: with memory | answers | gives first | tolerates k | window w]; who gives [state: all | a thin withholding | total withholding]. Laws: kept (Tolerance.total_stays; waitsAll_never_restores), arrives from any start (restores_from; gives_without_chain 'from L on'), border (restores_iff: no clear chain of n waits), a push taken back (thin_absorbed, the twin of C's perturbation_absorbed), clock (w consecutive errors), built cases. 'Restoring needs another law' is C's 'only a change of how the rule reads leaves'. With `hold` as one answer type, mutual giving kept, total withholding kept and a lock are the same kind of area, which is the non-dual point made by the structure. Strain: 'no chain of L waits' is a fact about the case's web with a number in it, so answers need parameters.

A, Absorption and ending (29 dynamics): holds, in two different ways. (1) The models (margin-of-a-regime, cascade, reserve, consumption-ends-with-feeders) are level against threshold [above | below | at nothing], fed or unfed, reserve; exact thresholds are borders, 'ends within the reserve' is a clock. (2) About eight dynamics quantify over ANY region (attraction-is-not-returning: `Absorbing`, `DrawnInto`; not-going-out-of-a-region; what-a-gate-keeps; every-loss-passes-a-juncture). They do not sit on a sheet: they are the legend, the proved meaning of outline, arrow and branch, said once. The theory already has formal words for a map; the store should use them.

Where it breaks or bends
- Cascades and co-ending run along the case's web. The condition is per formation, so a case with many formations has a sheet per role, joined by its couplings, not one position. `of` carries this; a single box per whole system cannot.
- A sixth and seventh shape were needed beyond the capture region (by chance; loop onset, 3 transitions). Shapes are a short open list, not five.
- F and H I read by title only. Cycles should be one kept area (family A: one cycle per basin), where a flat map would draw a ring of places; I have not checked this against their laws.
- Atlas-wide, half the exits are single built cases. Any honest sheet will be half dotted. That is the state of the work, and it should show.
first_change:
Give each of the 88 decisions three typed fields read from the Lean statement, not from the atlas sentence: `given`, `then` (answers to the seven questions) and `shape`; and add the mechanism laws that arrive or keep (uniform_locks, favouring_locks, drawn_locks, locked_stays) as rows beside the exits. Leave places-v1 as labels over combinations and leave the drawing as it is for now.

If even that is too much for one change, do it for one predicate: the hold. Re-point every law whose Lean conclusion is `Locked`, for either side, to one answer `held (side)`. That alone puts arrivals on the centre of the map, turns nine drawn movements into borders once `shape` is read, removes the terminus named for a good outcome, and shows the loop. It can be checked against the picture Ren has already seen.
false_premise:
Two, and a smaller third.

1. 'The data structure that projects onto the map' treats store and picture as one thing to optimise. They answer to different counts: the store to faithfulness, economy, scaling and many drawings; the picture to a person's five minutes. v1 ties them (one stored row is one box; relations and arrow labels live in layout.json), so each improvement to one costs the other. Separate them and the question splits. Is the store on the frontier? No: a typed store regenerates v1's picture and more. Is the picture? Not shown either way.

2. 'Optimal for human understanding' cannot be settled by a designer. A frontier is a set, not a point, and which point to take depends on what Ren weighs. What can be said is dominance on stated counts. The five-minute and one-hour counts are settled only by people reading; the whole-picture note already says so, and I would hold this proposal to it.

3. 'Places' as the missing middle layer is nearly right. The Lean's middle layer is predicates on a product (regions that overlap), and family A already proves what a kept region, being drawn in and a juncture are. A separate vocabulary for the map (place, arrow, stays, inside, leads-out) duplicates the theory's own.
